title: On the usage of the squamate integumentary system in a phylogenetic context, and a call to action
content:
Abstract
Morphological diversity in squamate reptiles is well documented. Despite large studies using osteological, physiological, and genomic data to infer phylogenies of the monophyletic order Squamata, the use of integumentary characters has been few and far between. This investigation serves as a preliminary foray into the possible use of scale morphology to address phylogenetic conflicts. Multiple correspondence analysis (MCA, a similar method to principal components analysis) was used to identify trends in scale morphology, and a chronophylomorphospace was also applied to visualize the development and divergence of these larger squamate groups in relation to the MCA results. Clusters visualized in three-dimensional morphospace challenge the assumption that scale morphology is too homoplastic to contribute to phylogenetic discussions of Squamata. Further application of this early dataset will illuminate areas of research not yet thoroughly documented with regard to the scale morphology of several higher level squamate clades. Consistent patterns within such clades may reveal selective pressures from habitat or locomotion on many regions of the integument. The importance of yet unexplored sources of morphological diversity is emphasized as a tool for justifying species delineation, especially in cases where molecular data is rare.
